title: Finite-population completion approximates automaton terminal laws uniformly in horizon
claim_groups: Two-sided terminal-law approximation with errors d/(2P) and d/(P alpha+d), uniform in the horizon, while repairing all one-coordinate input marginals exactly.

Binary-horizon terminal optimization, computable arbitrary-horizon optimal error, a compressed exact-marginal coupling with exact terminal evaluation and consistent coordinate queries, and a PSPACE upper bound for promised positive-gap decisions.

Fixed-order overlapping block-statistics and forbidden-local-pattern extension with additional denominator costs; no implementation is claimed for this extension by the one-coordinate diagnostic solver.
scoped_limitations: The PSPACE result is membership only; no hardness or exact threshold-attainment algorithm is claimed.
Compilation may be expensive in automaton dimension, accuracy, and rational denominator; the theorem is not jointly polynomial in all input parameters.
Arbitrary correlations with unconditional one-coordinate marginals are allowed; fixed stochastic kernels, blind independence, and exact accepting-support constraints are outside the theorem.
Internal proof reconstruction and reported exact-rational replay are source-reported; no independent mathematical reconstruction or research-script replay occurred in this intake.

related_cards.relation: Related finite-semigroup research only. N698 is an automaton-level, horizon-uniform approximation/compiler result; it does not replace N674's exact full-support commutative transport classification or resolve exact cutpoints.
